issue: #1919 split-identity pool rows — the sport-segment class, PARK-only
note: This file IS the scope. relocate-pool-rows-by-list.cjs touches exactly these ids and nothing else. Every entry was classified from the 2026-09-07 whole-corpus census (16,596,692 rows walked, READ ONLY) and its destination was checked live against card_catalog. Part 2 of 4 — the class is split across 4 files only to keep each list reviewable in a diff; each file is an independent scope.
rulings: CF-A-SPLIT-ROW-POLLUTES-TWO-POOLS. 94,275 rows of 16,596,692 carry a cardId whose sport segment differs from their hobbyiqCardId. The exact-pool reader ORs the two fields, so each such sale is read into TWO pools and prices a card it is not.

PARK, NOT RELOCATE — the destination does not exist. All 1,218 distinct pokemon destinations for this class are ABSENT from card_catalog (batched IN-query, read-only 2026-09-07). Relocating 7,996 sales onto slugs no checklist names would mint 1,218 identities whose only evidence is the sales themselves, which CF-CATALOG-MATCH-IS-SELF-CONFIRMING forbids. The rows are marked identityUnverified, which keeps them out of EVERY pool without asserting which card they belong to.

hobbyiqCardId IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY THE WINNER. Measured on same-setKey sport splits with an unambiguous setKey tell: hobbyiqCardId is correct 2,330 times and cardId is correct 1,203 times. A blanket REPOINT toward hobbyiqCardId would therefore corrupt roughly a third of the class. This list is deliberately narrowed to the ONE sub-class where the setKey itself proves the vertical — an unambiguous Pokemon TCG set — and every other slug segment already agrees.

THE EMITTER IS STILL LIVE. 3,398 rows carrying this defect were written in the 7 days before the census. recordSoldComp (soldCompsStore.service.ts) stores the CALLER's cardId verbatim while deriving hobbyiqCardId itself, and no write-time guard compares the two. This list repairs stored rows only; it does not stop the source.
